method: U1 (audit/AUDIT-1.2.42.md 11.2). Static reading of b5a29e73's source (identical on claude/audit-119): every cited line opened, the callers and guards around it grepped across scripts/, the tier files grepped for a test that pins the opposite. No harness, suite, scenario, probe or npm run; a short read-only node run of case-layout.mjs over hand-built graphs was refused by this session's permission layer, so finding 1 rests on reading alone. base-run.json was not present when looked for; no test result is cited as read.

checked.claim: Two counters refuting each other (or a counter refuting a deduction that rests on it) send layoutCase into endless recursion, and the Investigation panel can no longer open in its default Map view on any GM.
checked.why: Read the whole road. The cycle check takes `input` edges only (case-layout.mjs:90-92), so A refutes B / B refutes A, or C an input of D with C refuting D, passes it. depthOf memoises only after the recursion returns (case-layout.mjs:108), and a counter with no inputs takes its depth from its refutes targets (103-105): depthOf(A) -> depthOf(B) -> depthOf(A) ... with nothing in `depth` yet, so the stack overflows. The write road has no guard: the Refutes list offers every other non-evidence node, counters included (investigation.mjs:1473-1475), applySchemaSave writes the union of the ticks (1584-1587), setCaseNode checks only the row's shape (case-schema.mjs:428-437), graphOf keeps every refutes edge whose target exists (case-schema.mjs:342-345), and checkCase's only counter rule is noTarget (case-schema.mjs:569). caseMapRegion calls layoutCase with no try (investigation.mjs:1148) while the window's body is built; the view is the User's flag with `map` as default (investigation.mjs:1103-1106, 2268). The GM panel's tile catches the throw and says DRPG.Panel.failed (gm-panel.mjs:607-612), so the tile answers 'failed' as the finding says. Other roads looked for: api.mjs:886 exposes `investigationDashboard`, whose `view` argument opens the Table - a console road only, as the reader said; moveCaseNode (investigation.mjs:1930) and the trial console (case-trial.mjs:66) call the same layoutCase and fail with it, the console's mount being caught (trial-floor-ui.mjs:1637-1638). No tier test lays out a loop of refutes (R3375 at tests-tier0.mjs:24285 tests a cycle of inputs only, line 24323). The break lasts while the clock stands in the chapter that holds the loop (mapChapterOf, investigation.mjs:1121-1125), i.e. for that chapter's investigation and trial. Major kept: a GM's ordinary planning ticks lock the panel for every GM with no way back in the interface.

checked.claim: Every read of the server copy runs Restore's preview, which clones the whole store once per row (quadratic), stalling the primary for a second or more about once a minute late in a season.
checked.why: The mechanism stands as read: restoreCase computes previewSection for every backed-up store before it merges, with no branch on `quiet` (gm-stores.mjs:2455), and a quiet read uses only `beforeCutKeys` when `beforeCut` is set (2458) - never on the copy's road (case-copy.mjs:151). previewSection runs mergeSections(base, one) once per key of the file (gm-store.mjs:504-506), and mergeSections starts with a structuredClone of the whole base (gm-store.mjs:149, 330), so the work is rows x size. The read precedes every write (case-copy.mjs:177), debounced 15 s / at most 60 s (case-copy.mjs:51-52, 215), on the primary (218). What is not established is the failure scenario's size: the reader's timings are a Node run on built rows outside the harness (not evidence class H), and its own figure at 300 answer-key rows is 126 ms; a stall of a second needs about 600 rows in one store, a count no recorded reading of a real world gives (LIVE-E111-01 open). The one store with no bound at all, the balance log (gm-stores.mjs:1700-1711), is off by default. A real waste, quadratic, on the primary's main thread - in a large world. Lowered to minor: wrong in a particular situation (a large store), not shown in an ordinary one.

checked.claim: The server copy puts back the tombstones compaction removed, at each load, and the quiet read then counts as a change that resends the players' copies and runs the Faint pass.
checked.why: compact deletes old tombstones from this browser's section and sends nothing (gm-store.mjs:1070-1076). The file is built from the sections as held (gm-stores.mjs:2230-2233, 2270-2276), tombstones included; fileSection empties `d` only for another world (gm-store.mjs:534). mergeInto takes the max of the two `d` stamps and keeps it above the watermark (gm-store.mjs:317-319), and counts the key as changed when [e, t, d] differs (321), so the tombstone comes back as a change. restoreCase's quiet branch skips afterRestore only when nothing changed (gm-stores.mjs:2473), and the Faint pass runs when any store took something (2477-2482). The write after it finds the file 'same' (case-copy.mjs:183), so the file never loses them. Either order of copy read and compaction at hydration ends the same. Nothing in case-copy.mjs or the compaction mentions the copy (grep 'tombstone|compact' in case-copy.mjs: none). Once per load per GM (the compaction runs at hydration, gm-stores.mjs:2024), as the finding says. Minor kept.

checked.claim: When players are let into the file browser, the copy already on the server stays, and no text tells the GM it is there or within a player's reach.
checked.why: The module's half is confirmed: a refusal only counts, records and tells (case-copy.mjs:170-175, 203-207, 263-267); nothing deletes the file, and the header says why (FilePicker has no delete, case-copy.mjs:24-25). The three texts say only that no copy is written (lang/en.json:7210-7212), and the handbook's paragraph says 'the module writes no copy while that setting is off' (gm-handbook.en.md:1415), which a GM may read as 'there is no copy'. The stage's own default, 'the GM removes an old file by hand if a player could have listed it' (docs/dev/e111/STATUS-115.md:72-74), is said nowhere a GM reads. Weakened, not refuted: the step that makes it a leak - a player's account with FILES_BROWSE listing worlds/<id>/drpg-case on 14.370 - is LIVE-E111-02, open, and the handbook does tell the GM 'Never give players those permissions while the copy is in use'. The reader marked it suspected; it stays a question with that live check. Minor kept (it would be a blocker only once LIVE-E111-02 reads the listing as allowed).

checked.claim: A second body announced while the first planned Autopsy is still being issued is dropped by the `sending` guard, and its planned Autopsy is never sent.
checked.why: The code road is as described: the hook does not await (case-realize.mjs:208-210), a call while the chapter is in `sending` returns 0 (257), the first call walks only the `due` it read with the bodies found at that moment (258-262), and sendPlannedAutopsy has no other caller (grep: the hook alone) and no later sweep. A two-body chapter has no third discovery to pick it up. What is not established is that the window opens at a table: the second discovery must be stamped while issueAutopsy runs for every living student, and announceBody waits for the writer's waitUntil listeners (body.mjs:563-580, up to BODY_ANNOUNCED_WAIT_MS) before the next discovery's gather can follow - a timing no reading records. The GM can send it by hand from the GM panel's window. The reader marked it suspected; it stays so. Minor kept.

severity_changes: domain-case-f-planner-stores-2 major -> minor: the quadratic preview is real, but a stall of a second needs about 600 rows in one store, a size no real world's reading gives (LIVE-E111-01 open); the reader's own 300-row figure is 126 ms, and the only unbounded store (balanceLog) is off by default.
not_established: Finding 1 was not run: a read-only node run of case-layout.mjs over two hand-built graphs was refused by this session's permission layer. The verdict rests on reading case-layout.mjs:85-111 whole; the reader's own Node run (scratchpad layout-probe.mjs) is not a harness result either.

Finding 2: how many rows each backed-up store holds in a late-season world, and the time of one copy read on the primary at a table (LIVE-E111-01). A new live check: on a world after several chapters, time game.drpg's copy read (writeServerCopy with explicit) on the primary with the browser's profiler, and count the rows of the traces', bullets' and keyPlan stores.
Finding 5: whether 14.370 lets an account with FILES_BROWSE list worlds/<id>/drpg-case (LIVE-E111-02). If it does, the finding is a blocker (the whole case readable); if it does not, a text nit.

Finding 6: the time issueAutopsy takes for a full class on a real server against the time between two answered discoveries (new live check: two bodies, two discoveries answered at once, both planned Autopsies written).

The stale_windows hints of the reader (trial console's schema not watching the traces' store, tokens, the bullets' store or the cast; the case window, the health window, the realization and summary previews read once) were not part of this check: they are hints for the refresh pass, not findings of this file, and none was given a severity here.
